title: Tensor computation from a specified bounded-above finite free sheaf resolution
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a site [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] and $B$ a sheaf of commutative rings, with its category of module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Let $K^\bullet$ be a cochain complex [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules] with $K^i=0$ for $i>b$ for some integer $b$, and supply isomorphisms $\theta_i:K^i\xrightarrow{\sim}B^{r_i}$ with each $r_i$ a finite nonnegative integer and $r_i=0$ for $i>b$. Then every $K^i$ is flat [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules], and $K^\bullet$ is K-flat [def-pc-kflat-complex]. Suppose $M$ is a $B$-module sheaf and $\epsilon:K^\bullet\to M[0]$ a quasi-isomorphism [def-pc-quasi-iso-modules]. For every $B$-module sheaf $N$, there is an isomorphism in the ordinary unbounded derived category [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]
$$M[0]\otimes_B^{\mathbf L}N[0]\cong Q(T_N(K)^\bullet),$$
using the K-flat derived tensor [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent], where $Q$ is localization, $T_N(K)^i=N^{r_i}$, and the differential is $\gamma_{i+1}(1_N\otimes d_K^i)\gamma_i^{-1}$. Here $\gamma_i:N\otimes_B K^i\xrightarrow{1\otimes\theta_i}N\otimes_B B^{r_i}\xrightarrow{\sim}N^{r_i}$ uses the sheaf tensor product [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], with last map $z\otimes(b_j)\mapsto(b_jz)_j$ and inverse $(z_j)\mapsto\sum_jz_j\otimes e_j$. Thus, if $\theta_{i+1}d_K^i\theta_i^{-1}$ is locally the matrix $(a^i_{kj})$, the differential of $T_N(K)$ is $(z_j)\mapsto(\sum_j a^i_{kj}z_j)_k$. The comparison is induced by the total tensor complex [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves] and the signed interchange $x\otimes y\mapsto(-1)^{pq}y\otimes x$ on degrees $(p,q)$ of resolving complexes. In particular two-term and degree-zero finite free resolutions give respectively the complexes $[N^{r_{-1}}\to N^{r_0}]$ in degrees $[-1,0]$ and $N^{r_0}[0]$, with these same transported differentials. No flatness of $N$ or existence of points of the site is assumed. If $0\to B^m\xrightarrow{f}B^n\xrightarrow{g}M\to0$ is a specified short exact sequence of $B$-module sheaves, then the augmentation $[B^m\xrightarrow{f}B^n]\to M[0]$ with degree-zero component $g$ is a quasi-isomorphism, so the preceding tensor formula applies to that very complex and its differential. Likewise a specified isomorphism $B^r\to M$ supplies the degree-zero quasi-isomorphism augmentation $B^r[0]\to M[0]$.
